_doc: Random events when exploring. An encounter is eligible if it shares a tag with the place's tags, the player's realm is within min_realm/max_realm (realm ids, optional), and blocked_by_flag (optional) is unset. weight is relative; 'kind' fortune/misfortune weights are scaled by the Fortune attribute. effects use the shared effect keys (src/core/systems/effects.gd) and are applied when the encounter happens. enemy (an id in data/enemies.json) starts a fight after the text, unless it is lethal and Deadly for the player, who then senses it and slips away. days = time spent. only_if_applicable: the encounter is only eligible when its effects can apply (e.g. a doctor only finds the injured). requires_flag (optional): only eligible once that world flag is set (follow-up encounters). choices (optional, W-004c, at least 2; the encounter itself then has no enemy): after the text and effects the player picks one of [{label, text, effects, days, enemy, requires: {min_realm, min_alignment, max_alignment, flag}}]; a choice is disabled when its requires fail or its effects cannot be paid; a chosen enemy is always fought (never evaded). Set flags in a choice's effects (set_flag) to unlock follow-ups.

encounters.text: You wander for a day. Nothing of note happens.
Deep in a gorge, a cliff face is scarred by a single ancient sword stroke. You sit before it for seven days, and the intent within the cut seeps into your mind.
A lightning-split tree, dead for centuries, has put out a single green shoot. Watching it, you glimpse something about life itself.
You spot a spirit stone glinting in a ditch.
A wild boar charges out of the fields!
A bandit steps onto the road, blade drawn.
A ragged old man shares a breathing method before vanishing. Was he an immortal?
You gather spirit herbs from the misty undergrowth.
Deep in the valley you unearth a centuries-old blood ginseng!
The mist thickens and you lose your way for a week.
Glowing eyes in the mist: a pack of mist wolves!
A rogue cultivator eyes your storage pouch and attacks.
You find a small spirit vein and absorb it before it disperses.
A wandering doctor tends your wounds and refuses payment.
In a teahouse you overhear rumours of an ancient cave on Azure Peak.
Your pouch feels lighter. A pickpocket!
You win a game of stone-gambling and crack open a raw spirit stone.
A stone-skinned ape hurls a boulder at you!
A cloud eagle dives from the heavens!
Watching the sea of clouds, you glimpse a fragment of the Dao.
In a sealed jade box beside a meditating skeleton rests a single fragrant pill. Its owner died waiting for a breakthrough; you will not.
Among the bones of a long-dead cultivator lies a jade slip.
A stone guardian awakens, its eyes burning with formation light.
You share your meal with a starving child. Their grandmother presses a few stones into your hand, and Heaven seems to nod.
A hooded peddler whispers of 'blood pills' that need no herbs, only lives. You walk away, but the idea gnaws at you.
The villagers hold a harvest festival and press rice wine and dew grass on you as an honoured guest.
You catch a thief fleeing a widow's house and return what he stole. She insists you take a reward.
A dying cultivator presses a pill into your palm: 'Bury me, and live well.' You give him a quiet grave.
You find a wounded traveller too weak to resist. You strip his pouch and leave him to the wolves. The mist hides your crime.
A white fox sits beside a purple cloud mushroom and watches you. You leave it a share and it bows its head before vanishing.
A pocket of miasma rolls through the valley. You flee, coughing, and lose days recovering.
A blood-path cultivator steps from the trees, licking his lips at your qi.
A jade-scaled python lies coiled around a spirit herb. It lifts its head as you approach.
A righteous sect patrol shares fire and rations with you. Their elder tosses you a pill for the road.
An abandoned altar still hums with slaughter-qi. You drink it in; the power is real, and so is the stain on your soul.
A clear night, a falling star. You sit through the dawn and your breathing falls into a deeper rhythm.
Hired thugs corner you in an alley, sent by a merchant whose goods you outbid.
Sparks drift through the grass: a flame-tailed fox bares its teeth over a patch of flame lotus.
The ground shakes as an iron-horned rhino lowers its head and charges.
The mist turns bitterly cold. Frost-silk threads tighten around you as an ice-soul spider descends.
A ragged swordsman blocks the road. 'Draw your weapon. Let my sword see what you are.'
An Azure Cloud enforcer seizes your wrist. 'I sense demonic qi on you. Come quietly or be subdued!'
A red-robed Blood Lotus disciple circles you, smiling. 'The blood pools are thirsty, and you look full of essence.'
A coffin lid slides open. A bronze-skinned corpse rises, its joints grinding like millstones.
Storm clouds gather out of a clear sky. A thunderwing roc screams and dives at you, lightning in its wake.
The herb valley falls silent. A toad the size of a house blinks at you over a thousand-year lingzhi.
A roar shakes stones loose from the ridge. The Black Iron Bear King has noticed you on its mountain.
A red mist rolls over the road and condenses into a Blood Lotus elder. 'Core Formation essence. What a rare treat.'
Wailing fills the cave. Pale shades part, and a crowned ghost king rises from a throne of bones.
A wealthy auction house leaves cast-off ore in the sweepings. You buy it for nearly nothing.
A wanted poster offers a bounty on a demonic cultivator hiding in the mountain wilds. Perhaps someone brave will answer it.
A white-haired hermit shares tea and a single pointer on the Dao, then waves you away.
On a frozen cliff face, an ice soul flower blooms. The climb is brutal but worth it.
A rockslide buries the trail and you spend days digging free.
Beneath a toppled altar lies a scripture written in dried blood. Its first line promises power at the price of life. You take it.
A demonic cultivator's remains still clutch a pouch of spirit stones. Taking them feels like a quiet pact.
Behind a collapsed wall you find a sealed alchemy chamber. Its owner crumbled to dust long ago, but a jade case on the furnace still holds a formula for the Core Forming Pill.
The lingering will of a dead alchemist begs for release. You chant until it fades, and it leaves its life's formula, the Core Forming Pill, as thanks.
A dead alchemist's spirit clings to his furnace, guarding a scroll. You shatter it, devour what remains, and take the Core Forming Pill formula for yourself.
Restless ghosts wail among the ruins. You chant until they find peace, leaving behind a small gift.
A pit of stacked bones whispers to you. Wrapped around a skull is a skin-bound manual. You pry it loose; the whispering turns to laughter.
You recognise a demonic sealing pit. You burn the cursed manual and chant a rite for the dead; the whispers fade and a faint blessing settles on you.
On a cracked altar rests a scripture that drinks the light. You know what it costs, and take it anyway.
You shatter the altar and seal the scripture's hunger away with your own qi. Sages would approve.
An old woodcutter watches you spar with the trees, laughs, and presses a bundle of leaf-pages into your hands. 'The forest taught me. Let it teach you.'
Halfway up a cliff you find stance diagrams carved into the living rock by some long-dead body cultivator. You pry loose the clearest slab.
You spend days helping wandering monks rehang the great bell of a ruined temple. Before they move on, the abbot gives you their Golden Bell sutra.
A demonic cultivator lies dead in the brush, a blood-soaked manual clutched to his chest. You pry it loose. The palm prints on its cover are still warm.
You find a dead demonic cultivator and the blood manual he died for. You burn it with him so no one else follows his path.
In a sealed sword chamber, nine frozen swords circle a jade slip. When you touch it, the swords shatter into snow.
Where an earth dragon vein breaks the surface, a stele records how an ancient master tempered his body in its flow. You take rubbings of every line.
A mummified demonic elder sits cross-legged in a burial niche, a silk-wrapped manual in his lap. You take it while the corpse's grin seems to widen.
You find a demonic elder's corpse festering with corpse qi and burn it, manual and all, before it can rise. Your own qi is cleansed in the flames.
Deep in the cave lies the tomb of an Azure Heaven sword sect patriarch. His sword intent tests you for five days, then yields its canon.
A black bone slip floats above a pit of shrieking souls. You reach through their screams and close your hand around it.
You crush the bone slip that binds a pit of tormented souls. They rise in a stream of light, and some of their gratitude flows into you.
Empty chambers and dust. Whatever was here is long gone.
A fallen talisman master's pouch lies in the grass, its owner long gone. A few talismans inside are still potent.
A Daoist altar still hums with stored lightning. Beside it, sealed in oiled cloth, lie unused talismans and fresh gold-thread paper.
A sword cultivator sits dead in meditation, a sheaf of talisman paper across his knees. His last sword intent is folded into the pages, with notes on how it was done.
A landslide has bared a seam of black profound iron. You spend days prying it loose with your bare qi.
A weathered grave marker reads 'Spear Saint Han'. You sweep the grave and kneel. A spear rises from the earth and settles in your hands, as if it had been waiting for a worthy heir.
A lonely grave marker reads 'Spear Saint Han'. The dead need nothing. You dig him up and take his spear and burial stones.
Deep in the ruins an ancient forge still burns with dragon fire. On its anvil lies a jade slip of forging memories and two ingots of red-veined gold.
In a clearing where nothing grows, a crimson saber stands buried to the hilt in a mound of withered corpses. It hums as you draw near. You pull it free and feel it taste you.
A crimson saber stands in a mound of withered corpses, and you know its name: Blood-Drinker. You pour your qi into the blade until it cracks, and the souls trapped inside drift free.
In a coffin sealed with nine iron nails lies a corpse wrapped in grey silk that is colder than the stone around it. You strip the shroud from the dead and put it on.
A coffin sealed with nine iron nails holds a corpse wrapped in cursed spider silk. You burn the shroud with true fire and bury the dead properly. The tomb's stale qi clears.
At the heart of a sacrificial array a black banner flies in a wind that is not there. Ten thousand voices beg you to free them. Instead you pick it up, and they begin to scream.

At the heart of a sacrificial array a black banner holds ten thousand captive souls. You break the array flag by flag over seven days. As the last soul passes on, its gratitude settles on your Dao heart.
Wind tears the clouds open for a moment, and on a ledge no mortal could reach you see two snow lotuses white against the ice. You drift down on your qi and pluck them.
A faint pull on your spirit leads you to a crag where Nine-Leaf Soul Grass grows in the cracks of an old sword mark. You count the leaves twice before digging.
Beneath the cave floor the mountain's roots run with earth marrow. Pale fungus clings to them in clusters, and the air is thick enough to chew.
Above the cloud line you find a pool fed by snowmelt and starlight. A thousand-year lotus has dropped its seed pod; one golden seed still glows within.
An alchemist died here mid-refinement, her furnace still holding a soft grey glow. Under her hand is a jade slip: the Soul Nourishing Pill formula.

A dead alchemist slumps over a cold furnace. You bury her with the rites owed to a senior, and when you return the jade slip in her grave-goods glows warmly, offering you her Soul Nourishing Pill formula.
Grey fog rolls over the black water. You wade for two days among drowned banners and find nothing but leeches.
A still pool, cold as a winter grave, seethes with yin qi. You sit at its edge and draw the chill into your meridians.
Pale corpse-lilies bloom on a sunken war chariot. Purple mushrooms crowd its rotten wheels.

A drowned cultivator's body has washed up against the reeds, a sect token still in his fist. You carry him to dry ground and bury him under a cairn. His lingering resentment eases, and so does your heart.
A drowned cultivator floats face-down in the reeds. You cut his storage pouch free and push the body back into the dark water.
A corpse-refiner's disciple rises from the reeds, three bloated puppets shambling behind him. 'Fresh material!'
Beneath a toppled war altar the water runs red with the blood essence of ten thousand dead. You open your meridians and drink it in. Your qi swells; something in your eyes does not come back.

Beneath a toppled war altar the water runs red with old blood essence. You chant the rites of passing for five days until the pool runs clear, and the freed souls leave a trace of their gratitude in your sea of qi.
A blood-robed cultivator steps across the water without making a ripple. 'The marsh's yin qi is mine. So is yours.'
The water bulges. A jade-scaled serpent, older than the battle that made this marsh, rises from the deep.
Under a shell of rust lies a commander's sword hilt still bound in cold iron and a pouch of ancient stones that kept their qi through the centuries.
A silent ferryman poles you across a channel and refuses payment. 'The dead pay me already,' he says, and is gone in the fog.
A storm breaks over a bare summit. Instead of fleeing, you sit among the strikes for five days and nights, and somewhere in the roar you hear the heavens' grammar.
A single leaf drifts through the mist and never seems to land. You follow it for three days, and when it finally settles, so does something in you.
A shattered teleportation array still flickers in the rubble. Where its lines break, the far side of the hall is somehow one step away. You study the fold until you can almost feel it.
Ten thousand broken weapons jut from the mud where two armies of cultivators annihilated each other. The killing intent still hangs in the air, thick enough to taste.

choices.label: Drink in the killing intent
choices.text: You open yourself to it. Ten thousand deaths pour into your sea of consciousness, and you come out the other side colder and stronger.

choices.label: Chant sutras to lay the dead to rest
choices.text: For seven days you chant until the last angry ghost falls silent. The calm left behind is as hard as diamond.

choices.label: Leave the dead to their quarrel
choices.text: Some things are better left unlearned. You skirt the field and go on your way.

encounters.text: A wandering monk rings a cracked bronze bell at dawn. Each toll seems to strike your bones rather than your ears.

choices.label: Sit with the monk and listen
choices.text: Three days of bells and silence. When you rise, your body feels like a temple that no storm could shake.

choices.label: Walk on
choices.text: You nod to the monk and keep walking. The bell follows you for a while, then fades.

encounters.text: In a back street stands a smithy whose furnace has not gone out in three hundred years. The old smith lets you sit by it for five days; the flame never repeats itself.
Beneath a waterfall lies a boulder worn into a perfect bowl. You meditate under the torrent until you understand how the soft overcame the hard.
Locals swear the hill on the horizon was once a day's walk further west. You sit at its foot for seven days and feel it breathe, once.
An old woodcutter who has never cultivated a day in his life swings his axe without ever tiring. Watching how he breathes between strokes, you suddenly understand something simple and deep.
